issues.failure_explanation: Two stated characterizations of the tail constant B_ell are false as written. (i) The criterion integral_{|z|>eps} e^{k|z|} ell(dz) < infinity characterizes finite exponential moments E[e^{k|X_t|}], not 'finite moments of all orders up to k'; polynomial moments of every order are finite whenever the Levy measure has any exponential tail decay, as for all four experimental parameter sets. Hence k < B_ell is at most a sufficient (never a necessary) condition: e.g., the VG0 set has B_ell = sqrt(||eta||_rho^2 + 2 lambda) - ||eta||_rho = sqrt(0.2593 + 2) - 0.5092 approx 0.99, yet its moments of order k > 0.99 are all finite, contradicting the claimed necessity. (ii) 'B_ell >= 2 is necessary to guarantee the existence of a unique solution with finite variance' misstates a sufficient condition as a necessary one: SDE theory requires coordinate-direction exponential integrability integral (e^{z^i}-1)^2 ell(dz) < infinity, which holds for all four parameter sets (for VG0 the directional decay rates are approx 6.2 and approx 5.5, both > 2), so the solution is well posed with finite variance even though VG0's worst-direction rate B_ell approx 0.99 < 2 violates the paper's own standing assumption B_ell > 2 once the norm is fixed to ||.||_rho as specified in the experiments. (Moreover, because the norm is declared to be 'any given norm' and B_ell rescales with the norm, the blanket assumption 'B_ell > 2' as written carries no intrinsic content: any exponentially decaying measure satisfies it after rescaling the norm.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the two sentences and the assumption: state that the exponential integral criterion concerns exponential moments and that k < B_ell is sufficient (not necessary); formulate the well-posedness requirement as the sufficient coordinate-direction condition integral_{|z|>1} e^{2 z^i} ell(dz) < infinity (implied by, but not equivalent to, B_ell > 2 in a fixed norm), and note that all experimental parameter sets satisfy it.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification, scope, and internal consistency of the framework's Levy-measure assumptions are unreliable, and, read with the norm ||.||_rho used in Section 4, the VG0 experiment lies outside the paper's stated assumption B_ell > 2. No theorem, construction, algorithm step, or numerical result in the paper actually uses these statements (the scheme only needs the bounds (2.5), which hold, and coordinate-direction exponential moments, which hold for all four sets), so the method and all reported results are unaffected.
issues.title: Mischaracterized exponential-tail condition B_ell: sufficiency stated as necessity, moments conflated with exponential moments, and the standing B_ell>2 assumption fails for the VG0 experiment
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local rewording of two explanatory sentences and the formulation of one standing assumption; the numerical scheme, the appendix proposition, and every reported numerical result remain unchanged, all experimental sets satisfy the corrected conditions, and no advertised scope is lost.

Interpolation is performed by cubic Lagrange polynomials.

issues.failure_explanation: The interpolation matrices T^in, T^out (and T^SL) are defined as single matrices acting between two-dimensional grids (dimensions (sharp in)^2 x (N_x+1)^2 etc.) and the experiments use cubic Lagrange interpolation (P=3). Tensor-product Lagrange interpolation of degree P on a 2D grid uses a (P+1)x(P+1) stencil per target point, so the full interpolation matrices have up to (P+1)^2 nonzero entries per row (16 for cubics), not P+1 (4), and the matrix-vector multiplication costs O(MP^2), not O(MP). The stated figures are the one-dimensional values applied to the paper's two-dimensional construction.

issues.title: Incorrect sparsity and operation-count claims for the 2D interpolation matrices (P+1 instead of (P+1)^2 per row, O(MP) instead of O(MP^2))
